answer: One workable design: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because jade only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, oasis is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any opal approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
